summary.en: Choose writable character storage or read-only literal access, and use pointers to locate and process suffixes.
summary.bn: লেখা যায় এমন ক্যারেক্টার অ্যারে বা শুধু পড়ার লিটারেল বেছে নাও, আর পয়েন্টার দিয়ে স্ট্রিংয়ের অংশ খুঁজে কাজ করো।

notes: C string literals must not be modified in C89 through C23, even though their array element type in C is char. These examples target C17 and use const on pointer access paths to express the intended read-only role.

examples.title: An array copy and a literal view
examples.explanationHtml: The writable copy becomes Mab; the literal view still reads Lab.

examples.title: A suffix points into existing bytes
examples.explanationHtml: suffix selects the digits inside room. Its write changes both the complete string and the suffix view.

examples.title: Walk until the terminator
examples.explanationHtml: The full pointer walk counts six bytes. The suffix beginning at index three has length three.

examples.title: Writing through a literal pointer
examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined even if this declaration is accepted. Use char text[] for a writable copy, or const char * for a literal view.

practice.title: Print a checked suffix
practice.statementHtml: Read a word of 1 to 80 ASCII bytes and k from 0 to its length. Print Word and offset: then the suffix beginning at k.
hints: The terminator itself starts a valid empty suffix.

practice.title: Count letters using a pointer walk
practice.statementHtml: Read a word of 1 to 80 ASCII bytes. Print Word: then its number of alphabetic characters, using a pointer cursor.
hints: The cursor stops at the valid terminator.

practice.title: Mask digits through aliases
practice.statementHtml: Read an ASCII line of at most 80 characters and newline. Print Line: then the same buffer with decimal digits replaced by #, using a char pointer.
hints: Point into the writable array rather than a literal.

practice.title: Return the text after a separator
practice.statementHtml: For a nonempty ASCII code of at most 80 bytes, locate its first hyphen. Print Word: then the following suffix, or MISSING when no hyphen occurs.
hints: A final hyphen produces an empty but valid suffix.

quiz.prompt: Which storage can be changed safely by text[0]='M'?
options: A literal reached through a cast
quiz.explanation: The array owns a writable copy of the literal bytes.

quiz.prompt: Does char *p="Lab" make the literal writable in C17?
quiz.explanation: Literal modification remains undefined regardless of this non-const pointer declaration.

quiz.prompt: What does strlen(text+2) measure for a valid string with at least two bytes?
options: The suffix length from index two
quiz.explanation: The function starts counting at the passed address.

quiz.prompt: What happens to the original array when a writable suffix pointer changes a byte?
quiz.explanation: The suffix is a view into shared storage.

quiz.prompt: Which condition must hold before calling puts(found) after strchr?
quiz.explanation: A failed search does not return a valid string address.

quiz.prompt: Does sizeof p tell you the writable size of text selected by char *p?
quiz.explanation: The pointer stores no buffer-capacity metadata.

quiz.prompt: Can you free a suffix pointer into a local character array?
options: Yes if it points at a digit
quiz.explanation: The storage is not a dynamically allocated block owned through that address.

quiz.prompt: What separate strings result when only the writable copy changes?
quiz.explanation: The array and literal are separate storage.

quiz.prompt: Which complete room and suffix are visible after the digit write?
quiz.explanation: Both outputs share the edited digit bytes.

quiz.prompt: What lengths does the full walk and the offset strlen produce?
quiz.explanation: The suffix starts after the three letters.

keyPoints.en: A char array initialized from a literal owns a copy.
keyPoints.bn: লিটারেল দিয়ে শুরু করা ক্যারেক্টার অ্যারের নিজস্ব কপি থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Writing through a pointer to a string literal is undefined.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্রিং লিটারেলের পয়েন্টার দিয়ে লিখলে আনডিফাইনড বিহেভিয়ার হয়।

keyPoints.en: A suffix pointer shares storage with the original string.
keyPoints.bn: সাফিক্সের পয়েন্টার মূল স্ট্রিংয়ের মেমরিই ব্যবহার করে।

keyPoints.en: A pointer alone does not reveal writable capacity.
keyPoints.bn: শুধু পয়েন্টার দেখে লেখার জন্য কত জায়গা আছে জানা যায় না।

keyPoints.en: Check a search result before treating it as a string.
keyPoints.bn: সার্চের ফলকে স্ট্রিং হিসেবে পড়ার আগে NULL কি না দেখো।

examQuestions.question: Explain why char text[]="Lab" differs from char *text="Lab" when modifying a character.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The array declaration copies four bytes into writable array storage. The pointer declaration stores the address of a string literal. Literal storage has static duration but must not be modified. Prefer const char * for a literal view so accidental writes receive a diagnostic.

6 3

The suffix starts after the three letters.

examQuestions.question: For a nonempty ASCII code of at most 80 bytes, locate its first hyphen. Print Word: then the following suffix, or MISSING when no hyphen occurs.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void)
{
    char text[81];
    puts("Word:");
    if (scanf("%80s", text) != 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    const char *part = strchr(text, '-');
    if (part == NULL) {
        puts("MISSING");
    } else {
        puts(part + 1);
    }
    return 0;
}

A final hyphen produces an empty but valid suffix.
